# Suggested readings {.unnumbered}

Readings the group adds during the quarter, beyond the thirteen assigned pairs. Anything here is optional. A suggestion is not an endorsement, and nothing on this page has been through the [reading audit](https://github.com/Denolle-Lab/metascience-and-AI/blob/main/READING-AUDIT.md) that the assigned pairs went through.

Add an entry by opening a pull request that does two things: append the record to `references.bib`, and add a bullet below citing that key. Keeping both in step means every suggestion accumulates into the same [bibliography](references.qmd) rather than into a list of loose links. See [how to contribute](contributing.qmd) for the mechanics.

Say why it belongs here. One sentence on what the paper claims and one on which meeting it bears on is more useful to the next reader than a title alone.

## Suggestions

*None yet. The first entry sets the format for the rest.*

Here is the format. The first field is your BibTeX key prefixed with an at-sign, which is what renders it as a citation and pulls it into the bibliography:

``` markdown
**@yourkey2026.** [Paper title](https://doi.org/10.0000/example). Journal or venue. Access note.
— What it claims, and which meeting it bears on. *Suggested by Name, date.*
```

## Promoting a suggestion

If a suggestion turns out to be load-bearing, it can move into a session page as an optional extension, or displace an assigned paper in a later revision of the curriculum. That requires editing `curriculum.json` and the session file together, because `tools/validate.py` checks that they agree. Raise it as an issue first so the change is discussed before the syllabus moves.

## Related pages

Existing agent systems and benchmarks are catalogued in [prior art](prior-art.qmd) rather than here, because they are software and evaluations rather than readings.
